source_facts.name: Palladium
source_facts.state_name: Pd, Johnson, Matthey & Co. sponge, NBS XRD phase (1953)
source_facts.designation: Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd. sponge palladium
source_facts.sample_locator: Printed p. 21 / PDF p. 25, section 2.8 Palladium (Cubic): NBS sponge sample, supplier, spectrographic impurities and vacuum heating.
source_facts.density_locator: Printed p. 21 / PDF p. 25, section 2.8 Palladium (Cubic), final paragraph: density calculated from the NBS lattice constant, 12.04 at 25 degrees C.
source_facts.structure_locator: Printed p. 21 / PDF p. 25, section 2.8 Palladium (Cubic): cubic crystal structure and NBS lattice-constant determination.
source_facts.form: Sponge palladium supplied by Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd.; selected property concerns its NBS crystalline phase, not the bulk density of the sponge.
source_facts.purity: Palladium sample with NBS spectrographic impurity ranges reported in percent: Ag and Si, 0.1 to 0.01 each; Ca, Cu, Mg and Pt, 0.01 to 0.001 each; Pb, less than 0.0001. No mass/atomic percentage basis or total-purity value is established.
source_facts.processing: The sample was heated in vacuum at 700 degrees C for 15 minutes and rechecked; the source reports no appreciable change in unit-cell size. This heating temperature is not the density reference temperature.
source_facts.scope: The source sample is sponge palladium from Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd. Its reported impurities and vacuum heating qualify the NBS crystalline-phase result. No purity grade, lot number, specimen count, sponge bulk density or porosity is inferred.

source_facts.name: Silver
source_facts.state_name: Ag, Johnson, Matthey & Co. sample, NBS XRD phase (1953)
source_facts.designation: Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd., London silver sample
source_facts.sample_locator: Printed p. 24 / PDF p. 28, section 2.9 Silver (Cubic), left column: NBS sample supplied by Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd., London, purity statement and trace impurities.
source_facts.density_locator: Printed p. 24 / PDF p. 28, section 2.9 Silver (Cubic), final paragraph in left column: density based on the NBS unit cell, 10.500 at 25 degrees C.
source_facts.structure_locator: Printed p. 24 / PDF p. 28, section 2.9 Silver (Cubic), left column: face-centered lattice with four atoms in the unit cell, corrected lattice-reference temperature and NBS determination.
source_facts.form: The Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd., London silver sample represented by the NBS powder-XRD pattern; no supplier product geometry is stated in the selected sample description.
source_facts.purity: Silver supplied with a purity of more than 99.999 percent; the supplier spectrographic analysis indicated faint traces of calcium, iron and copper. The percentage basis is not stated; this is not a claim of exactly pure elemental silver.
source_facts.scope: The source-qualified Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd., London silver sample is distinct from the bismuth-rich silver comparison pattern discussed elsewhere in this section. The selected value is the NBS crystallographic density; no supplier lot, grade or specimen count is established.

source_facts.name: Tin
source_facts.state_name: White (beta) Sn, Johnson, Matthey & Co. sample, NBS XRD phase (1953)
source_facts.designation: Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd., London white tin; specially purified by Capper, Pass, & Sons, Limited
source_facts.sample_locator: Printed p. 24 / PDF p. 28, section 2.10 Tin (White or beta) (Tetragonal), right column: NBS sample supplier, purification, composition analyses and 12-hour anneal at 160 degrees C.
source_facts.density_locator: Printed p. 26 / PDF p. 30, continuation of section 2.10, left column above section 2.11: density based on the NBS lattice constant, 7.286 at 26 degrees C.
source_facts.structure_locator: Printed p. 24 / PDF p. 28, section 2.10: tetragonal white/beta phase; printed p. 26 / PDF p. 30, continuation: NBS tetragonal lattice parameters at 26 degrees C.
source_facts.form: Source-qualified white (beta) tin in the tetragonal phase, represented by the NBS powder-XRD pattern; no macroscopic product geometry is established.
source_facts.purity: Tin supplied by Johnson, Matthey & Co., Ltd., London after special purification by Capper, Pass, & Sons, Limited. The supplied analysis reports 99.997 percent tin by difference, with trace impurities; the percent basis is unspecified. This calculated composition statement is not an independent total-purity measurement or proof of exactly pure tin.
source_facts.processing: The sample was specially purified by Capper, Pass, & Sons, Limited; the purification recipe is not stated. It was annealed for 12 hours at 160 degrees C before mounting in the spectrometer. The annealing temperature is not the 26 degrees C density reference temperature.
source_facts.scope: One composition-level tin identity is represented by the source white/beta tetragonal state. Other tin allotropes, anneals and supplier records do not add identities. The selected NBS value is not the density of gray/alpha tin or an unspecified tin product.

identity_policy: Only Pd, Ag and Sn composition-level identities are proposed. Beta tin is the represented state, not an extra tin identity. Supplier, purity and heat treatment do not create identities. Root integration performs current-catalog deduplication.
